exercises.title: Difference quotient
exercises.prompt: For \(f(x)=x^2-3x+2\), calculate and simplify the difference quotient at \(x_0=2\), then determine \(f′(2)\).

steps: Passing to the limit \(h\to0\) we get the derivative at the point.

exercises.title: Three derivatives from the definition
exercises.prompt: Using the limit of the difference quotient, calculate the derivatives of: a) \(3x+5\); b) \(x^3\); c) \(1/x\). State the domain.

steps: The function \(1/x\) and his derivative have domain \(\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}\).

exercises.title: Tangent lines
exercises.prompt: For \(f(x)=x^2\): a) find the tangent line at \(x_0=3\); b) find the points where the tangent is parallel to the x-axis; c) find the points where the tangent makes a 45° angle with the x-axis.

steps: A tangent parallel to the x-axis slope zero: \(2x=0\), therefore the point is \((0,0)\).
A corner of \(45^\circ\) the slope \(\tan45^\circ=1\): \(2x=1\), therefore \(x=1/2\) and \(P=(1/2,1/4)\).

exercises.title: Absolute value
exercises.prompt: Study the differentiability of \(f(x)=|x-2|\) at \(x_0=2\) by calculating the right-hand and left-hand derivatives separately. Sketch the graph.

steps: We write the piecewise function: \(f(x)=2-x\) for \(x<2\), and \(f(x)=x-2\) for \(x\ge2\).
The two limits are finite but different: in graph an angled point appears.

exercises.title: A differentiability challenge
exercises.prompt: Study the differentiability of \(f(x)=x|x|\) at \(x_0=0\). Write the function piecewise and sketch its graph before calculating.

steps: The shape piecewise is \(x|x|=-x^2\) for \(x<0\) and \(x|x|=x^2\) for \(x\ge0\).
Both from left and right \(|h|\to0\), therefore the two limits coincide.
solution.result: \(\boxed{f^{\prime}(0)=0}\): the function is differentiable in zero.

exercises.title: Fundamental table
exercises.prompt: Differentiate: a) \(5x^4-3x^2+7\); b) \(\sqrt{x}+1/x^2\); c) \(2e^x-4\ln x\); d) \(3\sin x-\cos x\).

steps: a) We apply the term power rule by term: \((5x^4-3x^2+7)^{\prime}=20x^3-6x\).
b) We write \(\sqrt x=x^{1/2}\) and \(1/x^2=x^{-2}\): the derivative is \(1/(2\sqrt x)-2/x^3\), for \(x>0\).

exercises.title: Products
exercises.prompt: Calculate the derivative of: a) \(x^2\sin x\); b) \(e^x\cos x\). Clearly identify the two factors and their derivatives.

exercises.title: Quotients
exercises.prompt: Calculate the derivative of: a) \((x^2+1)/(x-1)\); b) \(\tan x\), rewriting it as \(\sin x/\cos x\).

exercises.title: Composite functions
exercises.prompt: Differentiate: a) \(\sin(x^2)\); b) \(e^{3x-1}\); c) \((x^3+5)^4\); d) \(\ln(\cos x)\). Identify the inner and outer functions.

steps: d) External logarithm, interior \(\cos x\): \(-\sin x/\cos x=-\tan x\), in the domain \(\cos x>0\).

exercises.title: Second derivative
exercises.prompt: Given \(f(x)=x^4-6x^2+1\), calculate \(f′′(x)\) and determine the candidate inflection points.

steps: Setting \(f^{\prime\prime}(x)=0\) we find \(x=-1\) and \(x=1\). The sign of second derivative changes in both.

exercises.title: Combined rules
exercises.prompt: For \(f(x)=e^x\sin(2x)\), calculate \(f′(x)\) and determine the stationary points in \([0,\pi]\).

steps: The product and chain rules give \(f^{\prime}(x)=e^x\sin(2x)+2e^x\cos(2x)=e^x[\sin(2x)+2\cos(2x)]\).
Setting \(\alpha=\arctan2\)in the range \([0,\pi]\) you get \(x=(\pi-\alpha)/2\) and \(x=\pi-\alpha/2\).
